turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I’m here because I keep losing my temper over little things. Like at work, I yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf, and afterward I was shaking. That’s really not how I usually treat people, and it scared me.

symptom_reasoning.S077: The patient reports repeatedly losing their temper over minor issues and yelling at an employee, which is consistent with irritable behavior and verbal aggression.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been acting impulsively in other areas of your life, beyond just getting angry?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself doing anything impulsive, like spending or taking risks or anything like that. It’s mainly been the anger that feels out of control.

symptom_reasoning.S041: The patient reports not noticing impulsive behaviors such as spending or taking risks.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your coworkers or friends would describe you as a hot-headed or aggressive person in general?
turns.patient_response: No, I really don’t think they would. I’m not usually hot-headed or aggressive. That’s why this has been so upsetting — lately I keep blowing up over little things, like that stock-shelf thing at work, and afterward I was shaking because it felt so unlike me.

turns.doctor_question: Have you always had trouble managing your emotions, or is this something that has developed recently?

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I’ve been really upset and not feeling like myself, but I’m not sure it’s sadness exactly.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to act on?
turns.patient_response: No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had upsetting thoughts, but not like urges I feel I have to act on. At least not that I’ve noticed.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and won't go away?
turns.patient_response: Yes. The fire keeps coming into my head when I’m not even thinking about it. Like I’ll pick up a pan, or even just be looking at a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m right back there—smelling smoke and seeing the kitchen filling up. It’s like I can’t stop it once it starts.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient describes recurrent, involuntary distressing recollections of the fire with sensory re-experiencing (smelling smoke and seeing the kitchen) that arise unexpectedly and feel difficult to stop.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when you have these angry outbursts or the recurring thoughts of the fire?
turns.patient_response: Yeah… sometimes. It’s not always during anger, but when those thoughts come up, or even when I’m just walking through the store, it can feel like I’m watching myself from a few feet away. Like the aisles and the customers are there, but they don’t feel totally real, and I’m just moving through everything on automatic.

symptom_reasoning.S082: The patient reports sometimes feeling as though they are watching themselves from a few feet away and that surroundings do not feel fully real, consistent with depersonalization/derealization.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me more about the fire that keeps coming into your head?
turns.patient_response: It just comes into my head suddenly. Like I’ll be doing something normal—picking up a pan, or opening a spreadsheet at work—and then it’s like I’m back there. I can smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up, and it happens before I can stop it. It’s really hard to shake once it starts.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient describes recurrent, involuntary fire-related memories with sensory re-experiencing (smelling smoke and seeing the kitchen fill up) that occur suddenly during ordinary activities and are difficult to stop.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of the fire?
turns.patient_response: Yes. I’ve been avoiding the house, mostly. I also can’t bring myself to open the mortgage folder, and even the herbs out on my patio bother me now because they remind me of that day. Anything connected to it makes my chest tighten, and I just… I can’t make myself go near it.

symptom_reasoning.S070: The patient explicitly reports avoiding the house, mortgage folder, and patio herbs because they remind them of the fire and provoke distress.

turns.doctor_question: Have your symptoms been causing problems for you at work or in your relationships?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s definitely causing problems. I missed a vendor meeting at work, and I actually walked out before finishing a shift because I just couldn’t keep going. And at home… I can’t face going back to the damaged house, so all the responsibilities there are just piling up. It feels like it’s getting ahead of me faster than I can handle.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing these angry outbursts and recurring thoughts of the fire?
turns.patient_response: It’s been about two weeks now. It started right after the kitchen fire, during that first weekend we were working on the house. Since then the thoughts keep coming back, and the anger’s been happening too.
